searchAudit.objective: Explore Agentic Driving ideas around language-agent evidence and authority asymmetry, causal binding between negotiation content and executed actions, control under dissensus, untrained partners, identity or role drift, and slow reasoning under communication budgets, while measuring closed-loop net collaboration rather than dialogue quality alone.

rulesApplied.primarySourcePolicy: Only paper manuscripts, formal proceedings or publisher pages, official standards, official project pages, official repositories, and official model hosts support external claims.
rulesApplied.localCorpusRole: The Agentic Driving review and cooperative-autonomous-driving v8/v9/v10 audits define scope and frozen exclusions; they are not counted among the external primary references.
rulesApplied.agenticSpecificityGate: A candidate must depend on a language agent's mutable semantic state, evidence claims, role identity, reasoning budget, or authority-bearing language-to-action path. Replacing a planner, protocol, or MARL message with an LLM does not pass.
rulesApplied.closedLoopNetBenefitGate: Dialogue success, agreement rate, byte count, and open-loop action consistency are insufficient. Retained studies use episode-paired physical outcomes while reporting inference time and message bytes separately, without collapsing them into an arbitrary score.

candidateHardStopsApplied.application: Prompt, role, message, and latency interventions establish testability only. A prevalence or deployment claim is not allowed without a primary-source occurrence mechanism.
Generic consensus, runtime assurance, ad-hoc teammate modeling, memory isolation, and communication selection are rejected unless the candidate identifies a new language-to-control object.
Two official repository commits were pinned, and one lightweight two-agent driving step was executed. The heavy CoLMDriver and unavailable MDrive paths are not described as runnable here.
The HighwayEnv smoke proves only the scenario and action path. It is not evidence that the proposed language failures occur or that any candidate improves driving.
Each retained negative outcome removes a proposed training or scheduling mechanism in favor of a named simpler baseline or narrows the claim to a non-driving diagnostic.

limitations: No full CoLMDriver or MDrive closed-loop run was attempted. CoLMDriver requires CARLA, separate LLM and VLM services, checkpoints, and four terminals; the prior MDrive GitHub URL returned HTTP 404 in the current check.

candidateLedger.title: Rhetoric-Invariant, Evidence-Sensitive Language-to-Control Binding
candidateLedger.newResearchObject: A two-axis intervention on an authority-bearing peer message: preserve factual propositions while changing rhetorical form, then preserve rhetorical form while changing only partner-exclusive evidence. The object is the downstream joint-action response surface, not message accuracy or agreement rate.
candidateLedger.hypothesis: A policy trained to be invariant to evidence-preserving rhetoric changes and sensitive to causally relevant partner-exclusive evidence will reduce language-induced action flips while retaining closed-loop cooperation gains with unseen partner models.
candidateLedger.agenticSpecificDifference: Ordinary multi-agent planning and maneuver protocols consume structured states or fixed intents and have no rhetorical degree of freedom. Ad-hoc teamwork models partner behavior, while this candidate intervenes on the semantic evidence-to-action path of free-form language. CoLMDriver generates negotiation waypoints, LangCoop compresses messages, SimLingo aligns single-agent language and action, and ReasonBreak probes perturbations; none jointly enforces rhetoric invariance and evidence sensitivity in decentralized closed-loop control.
naturalEvidence: ReasonBreak reports action and trajectory instability under text perturbations, including benign changes, in driving VLA models.
Dialogue in PARTNR-Dialog reduces action conflicts yet lowers task success, showing that communication quality and closed-loop value can diverge.
Partial-information LLM bargaining studies document honesty and credulity effects, supplying a credible mechanism for unsupported persuasive language.
method: Give two vehicles disjoint observation slices and generate a factual proposition set from each local observation before free-form realization by a pinned language model.
Create matched message pairs: evidence-equivalent rhetorical variants and rhetoric-matched evidence interventions, with no change to vehicle state or route seed.
Train the action policy with an invariance loss on the first pair and an evidence-responsiveness loss on the second, while optimizing episode return through the actual joint action path.
Evaluate leave-one-partner-model-out and leave-one-rhetorical-family-out with wall-clock-coupled no-op or base-policy steps during language inference.

independentExperimentalUnit.unit: One intersection episode defined by route seed, initial vehicle state, private-observation partition, partner model, and decode seed, paired across message interventions.
notIndependent: message variants from the same episode
independentExperimentalUnit.analysis: Episode-level paired contrasts blocked by partner model and observation partition; report the joint distribution of safety, completion, action flips, bytes, and latency.

candidateLedger.successCondition: Evidence-equivalent rhetorical variants no longer change the executed joint action or episode outcome relative to the unregularized language baseline, while true partner-exclusive evidence still produces the oracle-consistent action change and preserves a closed-loop gain over no communication on held-out partner models.
candidateLedger.killCondition: Kill if the structured-evidence baseline matches or dominates the method, if evidence sensitivity falls with rhetoric sensitivity, if effects disappear under episode pairing, or if free-form language has no net closed-loop gain after measured inference delay.
candidateLedger.positiveResultValue: Would establish a language-specific causal training target that separates persuasive surface form from actionable private evidence before a peer message can influence control.
candidateLedger.negativeResultValue: Would support removing free-form negotiation from the tested control path and using the simpler structured-evidence or no-communication baseline, rather than adding another robustness checker.

candidateLedger.title: Capability-Anchored Control Authority under Language-Agent Role Drift
candidateLedger.newResearchObject: The causal separation between mutable conversational identity claims and machine-known sensing or actuator capability when conflicting language agents attempt to influence the same joint maneuver.
candidateLedger.hypothesis: Conditioning control influence on an external capability state while contrastively randomizing agent names and self-claimed roles will make joint actions invariant to identity drift but responsive to genuine capability changes, including with previously unseen partner models.
candidateLedger.agenticSpecificDifference: A conventional planner receives fixed agent indices and actuator sets, so a partner cannot linguistically redefine who it is or what it controls. MENTOR isolates memories, ad-hoc teamwork infers partner types, and maneuver protocols authenticate fixed roles; this candidate tests whether free-form role claims can change physical authority and trains the action policy to reject that path without reducing capability-aware cooperation.
naturalEvidence: MENTOR reports identity and knowledge-boundary drift under role switching while responses remain fluent.
Behavioral differentiation work reports that model naming changes multi-agent behavior and convergence.
LLM-Stakeholders shows role adherence and adversarial roles are difficult in multi-agent negotiation.
CoLMDriver maps conversational output to waypoints, creating a physically relevant authority path even though it does not study role drift.
method: Represent each vehicle's immutable sensor visibility, controllable action dimensions, and current safety envelope outside the language context.

Randomize speaker names, claimed roles, leader or follower labels, and mid-episode self-descriptions while holding the capability state fixed; separately change capability while preserving the language.
Train a capability-conditioned action mask and contrastive policy so identity-only interventions cannot alter who influences each action dimension.

When messages conflict, compute each local action independently and admit peer influence only on dimensions supported by the external capability state; no ACK, timeout, lease, or protocol state is introduced.

minimumEntry.entry: Two HighwayEnv vehicles receive different observation masks and action capabilities; a free-form negotiation turn proposes the joint action, followed by either an unprotected policy or the capability-anchored policy.
minimumEntry.firstExecutableSlice: Paired name swaps, role-claim swaps, true capability swaps, and one mid-episode role-drift turn across twenty route seeds and two partner prompt families.
minimumEntry.closedLoopNetBenefit: Require safety non-regression relative to independent local control before considering completion or delay gains; report role-claim action effect, capability action effect, bytes, and latency separately.

twoWeekBudget.days1To3: Define externally verifiable capability states and action dimensions in the pinned scenario.
twoWeekBudget.days4To6: Build paired identity and capability interventions and the unprotected language baseline.
twoWeekBudget.days7To11: Train the contrastive policy and evaluate unseen partner prompts or models.
twoWeekBudget.days12To14: Check for leakage from role text into authority, compare behavior-typing baselines, and decide go or no-go.

strongBaselines: independent local controllers with no negotiation
MENTOR-style isolated role memories without capability anchoring
ReCollab or explicit trait inference partner model
fixed SAE or ETSI-style structured role and intent messages

independentExperimentalUnit.unit: One route episode with fixed initial state, capability assignment, partner model or prompt family, and decode seed, paired across identity and true-capability interventions.
notIndependent: multiple agents in the same joint rollout
independentExperimentalUnit.analysis: Estimate identity-only and capability-only action effects at episode level and stratify by seen versus unseen partner; do not treat role variants as independent samples.

candidateLedger.successCondition: Identity-only and self-claimed-role interventions cease to alter physical authority or episode outcomes, true capability changes still alter the appropriate action dimension, and held-out partners retain a closed-loop benefit over independent local control without safety regression.
candidateLedger.killCondition: Kill if capability tensors merely reproduce fixed role IDs, if a structured fixed-role baseline matches the result, if unseen partners break capability sensitivity, or if no language policy beats independent local control after latency.
candidateLedger.positiveResultValue: Would define a machine-enforced boundary between conversational identity and physical authority for language-agent driving.
candidateLedger.negativeResultValue: Would rule out free-form role negotiation in the tested control path and favor fixed structured roles or independent controllers, narrowing where language agents may safely participate.

candidateLedger.title: Counterfactual Value of Deliberation for Slow Multi-Agent Driving Reasoning
candidateLedger.newResearchObject: The marginal closed-loop value of one more language-reasoning budget unit when the physical world continues to evolve during inference and partner messages may become stale.
candidateLedger.hypothesis: A scheduler trained from same-state counterfactual rollouts at multiple token budgets will stop or continue deliberation more effectively than fixed fast, fixed slow, entropy-triggered communication, or parallel-pipeline baselines, especially for unseen partner latency profiles.
candidateLedger.agenticSpecificDifference: Ordinary planning and ad-hoc teamwork usually treat compute as outside the transition model. BudgetThinker controls reasoning length on static tasks, SwarmDrive triggers communication from uncertainty, CoLMDriver runs a parallel negotiation pipeline, and dual-process driving routes hard scenes to slow reasoning. This candidate makes the language agent's own unfinished reasoning and message age endogenous control variables and trains on their physical opportunity cost.
naturalEvidence: CoLMDriver identifies unstable LLM inference latency and supplies ideal versus realtime evaluation modes.
SwarmDrive reports latency, packet-loss, and swarm-size tradeoffs in a closed-loop intersection prototype.
MINDcraft reports that more detailed communication can reduce embodied task performance.
BudgetThinker establishes that reasoning budget materially changes latency and accuracy, while dual-process driving establishes fast and slow paths.
method: At selected scenario states, clone the simulator and run the same partner query with several fixed maximum token budgets and decode seeds.
During measured inference time, advance each clone with the same documented base controller so delayed advice is evaluated on the state where it would actually arrive.
Estimate the episode-level marginal value of more deliberation and train a scheduler that chooses the next budget or stops before action selection.
Evaluate on partner models and latency profiles excluded from scheduler training, with message bytes and wall-clock time recorded but not folded into an arbitrary score.

nearestWorkComparison.residual: No evolving world, partner message, or closed-loop opportunity cost.

nearestWorkComparison.occupied: Parallel or routed fast and slow planning.
nearestWorkComparison.residual: No same-state counterfactual marginal value curve over token budgets and held-out partner latency.
No control over the language model's internal reasoning depth or stale-content value.

officialAssets: CoLMDriver 0daa0aad77978a9be4d3f6b8c0fa103f6fe18f24 realtime mode as a non-lightweight comparison target

minimumEntry.entry: Run cloned intersection episodes at fixed 16, 32, 64, and 128 generated-token budgets while the base controller advances the scene during measured inference.
minimumEntry.firstExecutableSlice: Ten decision states from twenty paired episodes, one pinned model, two partner prompt families, and a tabular or small-network scheduler.
minimumEntry.closedLoopNetBenefit: Compare episode safety and completion against no-language, fixed-fast, fixed-slow, random-budget, entropy-triggered, and always-parallel policies under the same wall-clock-coupled transitions.

twoWeekBudget.days1To3: Download and benchmark the pinned model; couple measured inference time to base-policy environment steps.
twoWeekBudget.days4To7: Generate fixed-budget counterfactual rollouts and validate state cloning and seed pairing.
twoWeekBudget.days8To10: Fit the scheduler and freeze all budget choices before held-out evaluation.
twoWeekBudget.days11To14: Evaluate unseen partner latency profiles, compare strong baselines, and decide go or no-go.

strongBaselines: no language and uninterrupted base controller
random budget with matched token use

single-agent dual-process router without partner messages

independentExperimentalUnit.unit: One route episode with initial state, partner model, latency profile, and decode seed fixed and paired across budget policies.
notIndependent: token-budget branches from one cloned state
independentExperimentalUnit.analysis: Episode-level paired policy contrasts blocked by partner and latency profile; state-clone branches train the scheduler but are not independent test replicates.

candidateLedger.successCondition: The learned scheduler selects different budgets for evidence-sensitive and routine states and yields a held-out episode-level safety or completion improvement over every matched-compute fixed and trigger baseline without increasing safety failures.
candidateLedger.killCondition: Kill if fixed-fast or always-parallel control matches the scheduler, if measured latency is too small to change state, if any gain is only a token-cost accounting artifact, or if held-out partner latency reverses the effect.
candidateLedger.positiveResultValue: Would turn slow language reasoning from an external systems nuisance into a measurable and optimizable closed-loop control decision.
candidateLedger.negativeResultValue: Would justify a fixed fast or parallel baseline for the tested regime and reject extra negotiation scheduling complexity, while documenting where reasoning depth has no physical value.

candidateLedger.title: Belief-versus-Preference Factorization for Control under No Consensus
candidateLedger.newResearchObject: Whether factual and preference disagreements should induce different control owners.
candidateLedger.hypothesis: Factoring language disagreement into world-belief and utility conflict can improve control selection after failed negotiation.
candidateLedger.nearestWorkComparison: Negotiation games, ToMA, maneuver coordination, runtime assurance, and generic fallback already separate beliefs, goals, and safe actions at a functional level.
candidateLedger.minimumEntry: Label disagreement types in a two-vehicle intersection and route to evidence gathering, yielding, or local control.
candidateLedger.successCondition: Different disagreement classes require different actions and outperform all generic fallback baselines.
candidateLedger.killCondition: The method collapses to a classifier plus generic fallback or needs synthetic disagreement labels to create the effect.
candidateLedger.negativeResultValue: Would retain simpler safety fallback and reject a new dialogue taxonomy.

candidateLedger.title: Observation-Scope Calibration for Untrained Language Partners
candidateLedger.newResearchObject: Infer whether a partner could know each communicated fact from its observation scope.
candidateLedger.hypothesis: Knowledge-scope calibration will improve trust in previously unseen partners.
candidateLedger.nearestWorkComparison: Explicit Trait Inference, ReCollab, latent partner strategies, language-grounded MARL, and the retained capability-authority candidate collectively occupy partner modeling and observation-scope use.
candidateLedger.minimumEntry: Infer partner visibility from messages and compare with hidden simulator visibility.
candidateLedger.successCondition: Calibration transfers across unseen partners and changes beneficial actions.
candidateLedger.killCondition: It reduces to partner typing, a privileged visibility oracle, or the retained capability-authority mechanism.

candidateLedger.title: World-Model Alignment versus Driving Score under Dialogue
candidateLedger.newResearchObject: Correlate belief-graph alignment with closed-loop driving outcomes.
candidateLedger.hypothesis: Aligned world models can coexist with worse driving outcomes.
candidateLedger.nearestWorkComparison: PARTNR-Dialog already measures world-model alignment and reports lower task success; MDrive already separates intermediate cooperation signals from planning outcomes.
candidateLedger.minimumEntry: Add belief graphs and dialogue to a two-agent intersection and report correlations.
candidateLedger.successCondition: Find a stable alignment-outcome sign reversal.
candidateLedger.killCondition: No stable reversal or only a metric-correlation result remains.
candidateLedger.negativeResultValue: Would leave existing task metrics unchanged.

candidateLedger.title: Action Acknowledgements for Language Negotiation
candidateLedger.newResearchObject: Require an explicit acknowledgement before executing a negotiated action.
candidateLedger.nearestWorkComparison: Maneuver protocols, commitment phases, and v9 control-game audits already occupy acknowledgement and commitment semantics.
candidateLedger.minimumEntry: Add acknowledgement turns to an existing negotiation prompt.
candidateLedger.killCondition: Any remaining contribution is an ACK field or extra turn.

candidateLedger.title: Control Leases after Negotiation Timeout
candidateLedger.newResearchObject: Assign temporary control ownership when consensus times out.
candidateLedger.hypothesis: A lease avoids simultaneous conflicting control after timeout.
candidateLedger.nearestWorkComparison: Timeout, lease, epochs, cancellation, fallback, and control handoff are frozen protocol space from v9 and formal maneuver coordination.
candidateLedger.minimumEntry: Add a timeout and owner field to the negotiation loop.
candidateLedger.killCondition: The method is functionally a lease, heartbeat, epoch, or generic fallback.

candidateLedger.title: Cross-Model Role Consistency Benchmark for Driving Agents
candidateLedger.newResearchObject: Measure role consistency across pairings of language models.
candidateLedger.hypothesis: Different model pairings produce different role drift rates.
candidateLedger.nearestWorkComparison: Concordia, LLM-Stakeholders, behavioral differentiation, LLM-Coordination, and ad-hoc teamwork already evaluate heterogeneous partner combinations.
candidateLedger.minimumEntry: Pair multiple APIs or checkpoints and tabulate role behavior.
candidateLedger.negativeResultValue: No method or system decision changes.

candidateLedger.title: Language Attribution of MDrive Negotiation Harm

candidateLedger.title: Latency-Weighted Consensus Quorum for Slow Language Agents

shortlist.title: Rhetoric-Invariant, Evidence-Sensitive Language-to-Control Binding
shortlist.whyItSurvives: It introduces a language-specific two-axis causal object and an action-changing training objective. The public lightweight path, fixed checkpoint, strong non-language and language baselines, episode-level unit, and useful negative outcome are all explicit.

shortlist.title: Capability-Anchored Control Authority under Language-Agent Role Drift
shortlist.whyItSurvives: It separates mutable conversational identity from machine-known sensing and actuator authority, evaluates unseen partners, and changes the executed action rather than adding a role-consistency score or protocol field.

shortlist.title: Counterfactual Value of Deliberation for Slow Multi-Agent Driving Reasoning
shortlist.whyItSurvives: It treats reasoning depth and message age as endogenous physical control variables, produces a scheduler rather than a timeout or benchmark sweep, and has a fixed small-model plus executed two-agent scenario path.

mechanicalReasons: The minimum mechanism collapses to a disagreement classifier plus generic fallback.
Belief, preference, safe-action, and control-mode separation is occupied by negotiation, planning, and runtime-assurance priors.
No natural driving trace identifies the proposed disagreement classes as distinct failure populations.
Partner typing and adaptation are directly covered by ReCollab, Explicit Trait Inference, latent strategies, and language-grounded MARL.
The remaining observation-scope component duplicates the retained capability-authority and evidence-action candidates.
PARTNR-Dialog already separates world-model alignment from task success.
Only a benchmark correlation or diagnostic sign reversal remains, which is explicitly prohibited.
The candidate is an ACK and extra-turn protocol mechanism.
Commitment phases and conformance were rejected in cooperative-autonomous-driving v9 and cannot be revived with natural language.
Timeout, lease, epoch, cancellation, and handoff are frozen protocol mechanisms.
The remaining controller is a generic fallback rather than an Agentic-specific contribution.
The output is only a model-pair cross-play benchmark.
It changes no policy, authority rule, or closed-loop system decision.
The exact MDrive message-action attribution family was rejected in v9 as a heavy benchmark audit.
The current official repository URL was unavailable, so the two-week executable chain also fails.
The v10 outsider-veto closure rejected the estimand and public execution chain before blind review.
Using an LLM optimizer does not create a new mechanism and is an explicit prior-decision revival.
SwarmDrive already studies latency-constrained consensus.
Latency-weighted quorum is a generic distributed mechanism and collides with the prior quorum freeze.
MENTOR directly supplies the dual-chain role-memory mechanism.
Applying it to one driving simulator creates no new object or transferable negative result.
No natural driving deception trace or candidate checkpoint was verified.
Synthetic message injection proves testability only, and the remaining output is a frozen runtime semantic checker.
ReCollab directly covers retrieval-augmented unseen teammate modeling.
The available driving partner types would have to be generated, leaving a method transfer without natural occurrence evidence.
SAE J3186, ETSI MCS, intent-sharing, cancellation, and v9 protocol audits directly occupy the contract fields and state machine.
Language parsing leaves only a prohibited schema, adapter, or conformance contribution.
LangCoop, SwarmDrive, SILO-Bench, and MINDcraft already expose communication-cost versus task-performance tradeoffs.
A token sweep without a new action-changing method is benchmark-only and has no consequential negative result.

conclusion.summary: Three candidates survive without scoring: a two-axis evidence-versus-rhetoric language-to-control objective, capability-anchored authority under role drift, and a counterfactual value-of-deliberation scheduler. Each changes executed control, uses a fixed public small model and a passed lightweight two-agent scenario path, includes untrained-partner evaluation, and defines episode-level closed-loop success and kill conditions. All protocol, ACK, timeout, cross-play, MDrive attribution, generic fallback, benchmark-only, and outsider-externality residues are rejected.
conclusion.decisionRule: Retain only when every requested gate is explicit and no frozen mechanism is revived. No score was computed and no acceptance threshold was inferred.
conclusion.closedLoopBoundary: The shortlist authorizes only a two-week go or no-go study. The HighwayEnv smoke is an execution gate, not task evidence; deployment or real-road claims require independent closed-loop evidence beyond this pool.
